roles.name: Senior Software Engineer
roles.outcome: Lead ambiguous projects, write production-grade code, and explain system trade-offs clearly.

roles.name: AI Engineer
roles.outcome: Build and evaluate reliable AI applications instead of stopping at a model demo.

roles.name: Backend Engineer
roles.outcome: Design reliable APIs and data systems, diagnose failures, and defend operational choices.

roles.name: Data Engineer
roles.outcome: Build trustworthy data pipelines, reason about quality, and communicate trade-offs.

coding.label: Coding
coding.proof: one tested implementation you can rebuild and explain
learn: Study one reusable problem-solving pattern and write its invariants before seeing code.
Read a small implementation and identify its time, space, and failure boundaries.
Compare two solutions to the same problem and explain when each becomes the wrong choice.
build: Implement the pattern from a blank file, then add three edge-case tests.
Refactor a working solution for clarity without changing behavior.
Build a small API or command-line tool with validation and deterministic tests.
verify: Close every AI tool and reconstruct the solution from its invariants.
Create an adversarial test that would fail a superficial implementation.
Explain the algorithm aloud, including the first condition that would invalidate it.
interview: Solve a medium problem in 30 minutes while narrating trade-offs.
Take five minutes to clarify requirements before writing code.
Review your solution as an interviewer and list the strongest follow-up question.

debugging.label: Debugging
debugging.proof: one minimal reproduction and evidence-backed root-cause note
learn: Study the difference between symptoms, hypotheses, evidence, and root cause.
Learn one observability signal and the failure modes it cannot reveal.
Review a postmortem and separate contributing conditions from the triggering event.
build: Inject a reproducible defect into a small program and create a minimal failing test.
Add structured error handling and one useful diagnostic signal to an existing program.
Reduce a noisy failure to the smallest input that still reproduces it.
verify: Write three competing hypotheses before inspecting the suspected code.
Disprove at least one plausible hypothesis with evidence.
Document the causal chain and the test that prevents regression.
interview: Debug a broken function aloud without rewriting it immediately.
Explain what signal you would inspect first during a production incident and why.
Describe a failure you initially misdiagnosed and how evidence changed your view.

systemDesign.label: System design
systemDesign.proof: one architecture diagram and a short decision record
learn: Study one reliability or data-consistency trade-off and name the assumption behind it.
Trace a request through a distributed system and identify every state boundary.
Review a reference architecture and list what its diagram leaves unspecified.
build: Design a small service from requirements through API, data model, and failure handling.
Add capacity estimates and one explicit degradation strategy to a design.
Create a decision record comparing two architectures with measurable criteria.
verify: Attack your design with a traffic spike, dependency outage, and malformed input.
Identify the first bottleneck and show the calculation supporting it.
Remove one component and explain the new limitation rather than hiding it.
interview: Run a 35-minute design session with timed requirements, estimates, and deep dive.
Explain one trade-off in business language and one in engineering language.
Answer: what would you build first if the team and budget were cut in half?

aiFluency.label: AI collaboration
aiFluency.proof: one reusable AI workflow with an explicit evaluation check
learn: Study how task framing, constraints, examples, and evaluation change an AI response.
Compare retrieval, tools, memory, and fine-tuning as different system choices.
Learn one common model failure and design a check that detects it.
build: Ask an AI assistant for three approaches, then write the selection rubric yourself.
Create a reusable prompt with an explicit success test and refusal boundary.
Use AI to draft tests before implementation, then audit every generated assertion.
verify: Re-run the task without AI and compare the assumptions each approach missed.
Verify every external fact against a primary source.
Change one input constraint and confirm the output changes for the right reason.
interview: Explain when AI assistance increases risk instead of productivity.
Describe a workflow where the model proposes and deterministic checks decide.
Defend which data must never be sent to a third-party model.

communication.label: Technical communication
communication.proof: one concise project story or technical walkthrough recording
learn: Study a concise design document and identify how it separates facts from decisions.
Learn the Situation–Task–Action–Result structure without inflating personal impact.
Compare an explanation for an engineer, a manager, and a customer.
build: Write a one-page technical decision with context, alternatives, and consequences.
Record a two-minute explanation of a system you built using no unexplained jargon.
Turn a vague project claim into five specific, verifiable facts.
verify: Remove every adjective that is not supported by evidence.
Ask another person to repeat your main point after one reading.
Mark which sentences are firsthand facts, estimates, or interpretations.
interview: Answer one behavioral question with a clear individual contribution and lesson.
Explain a disagreement while representing the other position fairly.
Practice a five-minute project deep dive followed by skeptical questions.
